chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The believer is good in assistance, light in provisions, excellent in managing his livelihood; he is not bitten twice from the same hole.

key_terms.لَا يُلْسَعُ مِنْ جُحْرٍ مَرَّتَيْنِ: Not bitten twice from the same hole (metaphor for wisdom)

ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical signs and characteristics of a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith outlines the practical ethics of the believer, emphasizing financial prudence and social ease to avoid burdening others. The metaphor of not being bitten twice from the same hole underscores the virtue of wisdom (hikmah) and learning from experience, a key trait in Shia moral theology. This description aligns with the broader concept of the 'perfect believer' who balances spiritual devotion with worldly competence.
